subject: business-studies
title: Business Strategy: Corporate vs Functional
welcome_lead: Map how big-picture corporate aims cascade into functional plans across the firm.
meta_desc: A-Level Business Strategy: corporate vs functional strategy, mission, vision, objectives.
final_note: Strategy without alignment is just a slogan - link every department to the corporate aim.

concepts.def: Chandler (1962): determination of long-term goals and allocation of resources to achieve them.
Mission states current purpose; vision states future aspiration; both should anchor strategy.
1985: cost leadership, differentiation, focus; firms 'stuck in the middle' underperform.
Kim and Mauborgne (2005): create uncontested market space rather than competing in 'red oceans'; e.g. Cirque du Soleil.
Johnson, Scholes and Whittington: firms become misaligned with environment as historic success blinds management.
Corporate (which markets), business (how to compete), functional (operations) levels of strategic decision.

walkthroughs.body_html: Corporate strategy decides what businesses to compete in. Business-unit strategy decides how to compete in each market. Functional strategy decides how marketing, operations, HR and finance support that competitive position.

Corporate objectives (e.g. 10 percent revenue growth) cascade into functional targets - marketing might target a 5 percent rise in market share while operations targets a 3 percent cut in unit cost. Misalignment causes wasted resources.
Strategy moves from analysis (SWOT, PESTLE, Five Forces) to choice (Porter, Ansoff) to implementation (resources, structure, change management). Each stage feeds the next.
